v1.notes: Reproduces (not validates) Guo et al. 2026 obstructed-sky ratios from the USGS Gale 1 m DEM at MSL waypoint positions (MAE 2.0 pp over 15 periods, r=0.94). Metric definition chosen post hoc among 3 readings. Dose-drop RMSE 4.3 pp with our ROS vs 1.8 pp with the paper ROS; the largest miss is Maria Gordon Notch (narrow valley: ours 25.66% vs paper 37.9%). 8 events, one rover, one GCR model: indicative only.

v2.notes: Pandolf+Santee x g-ratio vs IST-2 Mark III suited VO2 (digitized Fig. 36 trend lines, Norcross 2010), 5 gravities x 4 grades, subject mass 80.7 kg, suit 121 kg, speed 0.765 m/s (paper range 0.56-0.97). Model underpredicts at 0.12-0.17 g (measured VO2 has a gravity-independent floor) and is within about +-14% at 0.22-0.32 g. 0.38 g is an extrapolation beyond the 0.32 g maximum; no data there.

v3.manualPlanningRef: no published figure found for hours of manual EVA traverse planning per EVA; only lead times (D-RATS 2010 planning began ~12 months before the field test; BASALT traverse targets were chosen months ahead from satellite imagery)
v3.notes: gale-v1 real DEM, base PR-1, 200 seeded scenarios (3-6 of 12 stations, start 08:00-11:00 LTST, sol 412 with assumed Ls 240). Nearest-first WITH the same safety check selected exactly the same station set as Marswalk in every scenario (ratio 1.0): in this tight-limit site the safety rules, not the stop-order optimisation, decide the outcome. The naive slope-only plan visits ALL requested targets and breaks >=1 hard rule in 99.5% of scenarios. Science values are the team STM heuristic. See v3_impact/README.md.
